findings.claim: The new debt row "ADR-021's published DOC_ALLOW count is stale again, 20 against a measured 26" mis-states the committed file: the same ADR sentence already publishes 26, and the row's assertion that "the prose count was not moved with them" is false.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:142 asserts ADR-021 "still reads '20 remaining legitimate non-measurements' ... while len(DOC_ALLOW) answers 26 ... and the prose count was not moved with them". But specs/decisions/ADR-021-benchmark-instrument.md:377-381 reads: "The 20 remaining legitimate non-measurements are listed in DOC_ALLOW with a reason each (len(DOC_ALLOW) re-measured 2026-08-23, L1, PR #12 R29 -- the count was first written as 14 from memory; **26 after D2**, same day: +13 dated entries, -7)". The count WAS moved, in the same sentence, and 20+13-7=26 reconciles. The residual real defect is narrower: only the sentence's lead integer is stale relative to its own parenthetical. A ledger row written to document a stale-number defect is itself carrying an inaccurate reading of the file it cites -- the exact class it names.
findings.repro: awk 'NR>=376 && NR<=382' specs/decisions/ADR-021-benchmark-instrument.md; python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from evals.bench import DOC_ALLOW;print(len(DOC_ALLOW))"  # 26, and line 379 already says '26 after D2'
findings.acceptance: The row states what is actually wrong -- the lead integer at ADR-021:377 disagrees with the corrected count in its own parenthetical at :379 -- and drops the claim that the count was never moved.
